installed_cold_coverage.claim_confirmed_for_manifest: run-2's cold arm (fresh writable NUMBA_CACHE_DIR per sample per tree) forces full per-process JIT compilation -- the dominant term of the read-only-installed cold cost. Both trees ship cache=True njit kernels, so the on-disk cache is real and its defeat in a read-only site-packages makes compile a genuine per-process user cost; a read-only cache additionally skips only the small cache-write I/O my fresh writable dir performs, so the model is conservative.
installed_cold_coverage.what_it_is_not: It is a MODEL on source trees, not a direct installed-tree measurement; F5's installed gates remain the separate direct installed record. And if a persistent writable NUMBA_CACHE_DIR is ever introduced (the recorded future work), 'cold' changes meaning entirely (observed in-process disk-cache load ~320 ms, run-1 analysis, vs compile ~2.4-2.7 s) and the gate would need its own record -- consistent with the original ruling's ground that the mitigation is new behavior invalidating evidence reuse.
